en: 3. The Question on the Factors of the Seed “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘two factors of the seed must be grasped,’ which are those two factors that must be grasped?
“Just as, Great King, a seed, though it may be small, when sown in a fertile field and the rain falls properly from the sky, will yield a very great abundance of fruit;”
In the same way, Great King, the virtue practiced by a yogin, a practitioner of yoga, will display only the fruit of recluseship.
This, Great King, is the first factor of the seed that should be grasped.
Furthermore, great king, a seed sown in a well-cleared field sprouts very quickly;

even so, great king, the mind of a yogi, a practitioner of yoga, when well-guarded and purified in an empty dwelling, when cast into the excellent field of the foundations of mindfulness, sprouts very quickly.
This, great king, is the second quality of the seed that should be adopted.
This was also said, Great King, by the Elder Anuruddha:
“Just as when a seed is sown in a perfectly pure field...”
The fruit for him is vast;
In the same way, the mind of the practitioner—
it grows very quickly in the field of the foundations of mindfulness.”
The third question on the limbs of the seed.
